title: The Empty Parish
premise: When the coffin of Hollow Creek's revered founder, Ezekiel Marsh, is exhumed for a bicentennial ceremony and found empty, true-crime podcaster Sable Sandoval arrives to cover the story, only to discover the town's oldest closed case — the 1923 disappearance of Ezekiel's wife, Adeline — is the key to everything. Sable's investigation reveals that Adeline never vanished; she fled an abusive marriage with the town doctor, and Ezekiel's descendants have guarded the empty grave for a century to protect the founding myth. As the trial of the gravedigger who 'desecrated' the tomb approaches, Sable must choose between exposing the truth and destroying the community that has finally made them feel they belong. In the end, Sable broadcasts Adeline's real story, the town fractures and then heals by reclaiming its honest history, and Sable realizes closure isn't ending a case — it's telling it right.
about_author: Sebastian Delacroix is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering cold cases across the American Midwest before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about the stories communities tell themselves and the price of the truth.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Sable Sandoval, riding high on a solved case and hungry for the next, receives a tip about Hollow Creek's bicentennial exhumation. Arriving in town, they feel the strange warmth of a place desperate to be liked. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: confident curiosity curdling into unease as the townsfolk seem too eager to control the narrative.

chapters.title: The Coffin Opens
chapters.summary: Before the whole town, the coffin of founder Ezekiel Marsh is opened to reveal nothing but century-old padding. The gravedigger, old Tom Vess, is arrested for theft, but Sable notices the seals on the coffin were intact. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the thrill of an impossible puzzle — a locked-room mystery in reverse.

chapters.title: Adeline's Portrait
chapters.summary: Researching the town archives, Sable finds the 1923 file on Adeline Marsh, Ezekiel's wife, declared dead after vanishing. Her portrait's eyes have been scratched out. The town historian, Ruth Calloway, warns Sable off with genuine fear. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: first inkling that the empty coffin is the newer of two old lies.

chapters.title: What Tom Buried
chapters.summary: Sable visits jailed Tom Vess, who claims he found the coffin empty decades ago while digging a neighboring grave — and resealed it, believing the town's peace mattered more than the truth. POV: alternating Sable and Tom. Emotional beat: Sable's professional creed — never take a case you can't close — collides with Tom's quiet moral compromise.

chapters.title: The Doctor's Ledger
chapters.summary: In a flooded cellar, Sable finds the 1923 ledger of town doctor Elias Wrenn, whose entries stop abruptly the month Adeline vanished — and resume in a town three states away. Bruises recorded in Adeline's visits tell the rest. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: horror and tenderness as the cold case turns warm-blooded: she ran from him.

chapters.title: Descendants of a Lie
chapters.summary: The Marsh family council offers Sable money and access to kill the story; council matriarch Vivian Marsh reveals the family has always known, passing the secret like an heirloom. Sable refuses, then doubts themselves. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging — they've never been wanted anywhere like this town wants them complicit.

chapters.title: Fire in the Archive
chapters.summary: The town hall archive burns the night before Sable's key episode airs; Ruth Calloway is hospitalized pulling out the last Adeline box. Sable realizes someone inside the investigation is feeding the Marshes their moves. POV: Sable and Ruth. Emotional beat: fear hardens into resolve; the case is no longer Sable's, it's Adeline's.

chapters.title: The Grave Next Door
chapters.summary: Following Wrenn's ledger, Sable finds Adeline's real grave under a different name in a prairie cemetery — and her descendants, who never knew the whole truth. Tom's trial begins back home as Sable records the testimony of the living past. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: grief and wonder; closure means finding where she actually rested.

chapters.title: The Verdict and the Broadcast
chapters.summary: At trial's climax, Sable plays the episode live: Adeline's flight, Ezekiel's violence, the century of complicity. Tom is acquitted as the courtroom turns on the myth instead. Vivian Marsh publicly breaks, confessing her grandfather's letters. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the climax — truth detonating a town's identity, love for the place warring with duty to the dead.

chapters.title: A Parish Refilled
chapters.summary: Months later, Hollow Creek buries Adeline's remains beside a new honest monument; the town is smaller, poorer in myth, richer in truth. Sable, offered a permanent place, chooses to stay — their first case closed not by an ending, but by a beginning. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted; love against duty resolved as the same choice.
